minor.title: Qualify parser/query reuse for notebook input
minor.reasoning: The new documentation broadly promises worker/language parser/query reuse. For .ipynb, BytesExtractor::extract_graph_facts immediately delegates to notebook::extract_notebook_file (tree_sitter.rs:418-420), which creates query_cache per notebook call (notebook.rs:81), uses it only for that notebook (notebook.rs:401-407), and parse_source constructs Parser::new for each cell/root parse (notebook.rs:595-603). The cached JupyterNotebook BytesExtractor therefore does not amortize notebook cell parser setup or query compilation across rows/chunks.
minor.reproduction: Source reasoning: evaluate two .ipynb rows containing a Python cell; each invocation reaches a fresh notebook query_cache and new per-cell parser, regardless of the worker HashMap entry. No runtime instrumentation or duplicate build performed.
minor.impact: No native parity, isolation or memory-safety defect; minor qualification of the spec's general reuse requirement/performance description.
minor.recommendation: Document the native notebook exception explicitly, or plan notebook parser/query reuse as separate work.

requirements_assessment.try_null_errors: NULL arguments short-circuit; successful empty inputs remain non-NULL; native errors map to SQL InvalidInput. All extraction/conversion precedes output mutation, so parsing/path failures do not leave partially appended output for TRY retry. Error retry may repeat parser work; exactly-once parser execution is not claimed.
requirements_assessment.oracle: Independent example writes fixtures under fresh non-Git temporary roots and invokes pre-existing build_facts_for_paths; it never calls new extract_file_facts. Exact all-five-collection/list-order comparisons, field-set checks, Some/None evidence checks, deterministic serde enum/f32 transport normalization, languages, local macro candidates/attributes, one-file unresolved references, IDs, constants/selected vectors/multiple chunks, oversize child lists and typed Parquet inspected.
requirements_assessment.sql: Physical staged-source DISTINCT and key-conflict/null checks; physical anti-join on (blob_oid,logical_path,extractor_sha) before scalar evaluation; typed result stored once, status projected later; separate five UNNEST tables preserve list ordinal and avoid Cartesian multiplication. Parent status retained for NULL/error/empty children. LEFT JOIN retains root/merge/duplicate/not_cached occurrence lineage. Typed Parquet snapshots readable without extension.
requirements_assessment.limits: Whole-file AST work remains scalar native parsing; no SIMD-AST or speedup conclusion. Adapter holds a chunk of owned facts plus output vectors; input bytes do not bound AST/output memory and Rust allocations lack a new admission/backpressure policy. Native structured-data cutoffs, cell-relative notebook coordinates and physical-Rust-only macro evidence remain native semantics. Single writer; all statuses incl errors cached until explicit deletion; schema migration explicit; children/snapshots rebuild over full cache; Parquet publication non-atomic after database commit.
